items.title: Samsung’s Phone app could start checking if calls from contacts are being spoofed
items.summary:
Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Samsung’s Phone app could soon warn you when a scammer is faking a call from your contacts. 
 The feature uses RCS to verify that the call is indeed coming from the caller your phone says it is from. 
 It does not share the caller’s details with Samsung’s servers, but will require an active internet connection. 
 The feature will not verify calls coming from unknown callers, but only the ones saved in your contacts. 

In June this year, Google introduced a mechanism to identify potentially harmful spoofed or fake calls on Pixel devices . That way, a scammer using a spoofing tool to make the call appear to come from one of your contacts could be easily discovered. The feature works on RCS, the media-rich texting protocol that allows instant messaging on Google Messages, to match the call’s origin to the contact’s device.

At the time of its release on Pixel phones, Google said it plans to expand it to other devices, and we’re seeing signs of that happening now, starting with One UI 9.5 on Samsung Galaxy devices.
items.t: Samsung’s Phone app could start checking if calls from contacts are being spoofed

items.title: How to pay with your Android phone anywhere in the world
items.summary:
Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority 

Google likes to make its products needlessly convoluted, and nowhere is this more evident than with Google Pay and Google Wallet. While one service would’ve done the job — like Apple Pay and Samsung Pay — Google has a confusing system that necessitates an article (such as this one) to decode.

Basically, Google Wallet is what you use to store payment cards, make in-store and online payments in the U.S. and other western countries. Google Pay itself isn’t available as a standalone app other than in India and Singapore, with Google shutting down the app in most global markets in 2022 and in the U.S. after 2024. Why did Google do this, you ask? Because it saw that Wallet was being used five times as much, so it folded in most features of Google Pay into Wallet. Now, Google Pay basically works as a transaction layer within Wallet.
items.t: How to pay with your Android phone anywhere in the world
